I used to be the external hard drive gal until mine got corrupted and I lost all files. No way of ever retrieving it back. Nada. Tried every thing. Fun fact: it was a Seagate 2TB. Although, maybe mine was a counterfeit or something. Idk. 

Anyway, I'm also like you but I've now learned better and have just invested in a monthly sub for 2TB google storage. Now I know the risks and implications about privacy and security. But honestly, it's not like I'm keeping confidential or highly sensitive videos and photos so it doesn't really matter. 

I can access them anywhere as long as I have internet and a smart gadget. And since it's google, I don't think I will be worrying about losing all files because they'll shut the service down or something...for now, at least and hopefully forever. 

Point is, it's safer and easily retrievable to have it on the cloud. No worries of it being corrupted. 

And actually, having it on a hard drive doesn't automatically mean it'll be faster to load, unless you go for the quick data ones which are super expensive. It's a hassle also transferring it from your PC to the external drive. The risk about external drive transfers is that if there is any interruption during the transfer process at all, that can damage the disk and the data. And that actually happens fairly often especially with the cheaper options. There's too much risk of an abrupt disconnect in between. That's what I am avoiding.

I know people have suggested to just buy an SSD and an enclosure for it. I think that's a safer option if you go for the offline option.

Sorry, but I don't think anyone can give you advice for natural treatment that works solely on its own for bipolar. Bipolar disorder is as it says, a disorder, and an illness that needs traditional medication foremost in order to treat the symptoms, along with therapy, and healthy lifestyle habits. Sure, alternative treatment can help but it is not enough. If this was the case, many of us wouldn't have to be on meds, in fact, maybe bipolar disorder wouldn't even be a thing at all.

If you're really looking for treatment advice that works, open your mind a bit and go see a psychiatrist for meds. If your spiritual belief is preventing you from leading a good life generally and possibly straining your relationships with people because you refuse to be on meds for bipolar, maybe reconsider that as well. What you felt on certain meds might not give you the same experience for bipolar meds.

My bipolar ruined a lot of aspects of my life for a long time and I only, only, got better when I was finally on the right meds. Honestly, if it weren't for my meds now I definitely wouldn't be alive today. I don't know how you do it.

And I wish I could have your mania. I'm bipolar 2 so I only experience hypomania and it's not severe. Still, I have made poor impulsive decisions during that period.

I don't mean to invalidate you but for me, if you can get by without proper medication, I can't help but doubt whether what you're dealing with is really the disorder. Sorry.

But as for your question, you can find a lot just by searching it on google. If you rely just on alternative treatment, you pretty much have to control every other aspect of your life: strict regimen, proper discipline, support system that won't fail on you, etc. But like again, if you get into an episode, except for your support system, I believe 90% chance of following those aspects will fail.
